segments.t: In the restaurant office, Chef Viktor Barinov urgently needs money to place a guaranteed bet on a football derby. He calls restaurant owner Dmitry Nagiyev, hoping to secure an advance, but Dmitry sees right through him. Listen to their phone conversation in Russian first, and then we will examine each sentence.
Дмитрий Владимирович, доброе вам утро!
Здорово, Виктор, денег не дам!
Я тебе две зарплаты уже выдал.
Чего ты хотел?
Да я не за деньгами звоню!
Да? А зачем тогда звонишь?
Сегодня вечером важный футбольный матч.
Опять твой любимый Спартак играет?
Да, и у меня есть верная информация!
Виктор, ставки на спорт опасны.
Мне нужен небольшой аванс до завтра.
Я знаю твои авансы, Виктор.
Ни копейки ты не получишь!
Дмитрий, ты пожалеешь об этом!
Now, let us examine the vocabulary and phrasing of this sharp phone exchange.
Дмитрий Владимирович, доброе вам утро!
'Dmitry Vladimirovich, good morning to you!' Viktor greets his boss on the phone with polite cheerfulness.
Здорово, Виктор, денег не дам!
'Hey, Viktor, I am not giving you money!' Dmitry immediately shuts down any financial requests.
Я тебе две зарплаты уже выдал.
'I already paid you two paychecks.' Dmitry reminds the chef of his previous advance payments.
Чего ты хотел?
'What did you want?' Dmitry demands to know the real reason behind the phone call.
Да я не за деньгами звоню!
'Why, I am not calling for money!' Viktor pretends that his intention is purely social.
Да? А зачем тогда звонишь?
'Really? Then why are you calling?' Here Nagiyev anchors the line on the word meaning 'why' and builds the thought around 'then' and 'are calling'.
Сегодня вечером важный футбольный матч.
'Tonight is an important football match.' Viktor tries to steer the topic toward sports.
Опять твой любимый Спартак играет?
'Is your beloved Spartak playing again?' Dmitry brings up the chef's well-known obsession.
Да, и у меня есть верная информация!
'Yes, and I have reliable insider info!' Viktor hints at his guaranteed secret source.
Виктор, ставки на спорт опасны.
'Viktor, sports betting is dangerous.' Dmitry warns his impulsive head chef against gambling.
Мне нужен небольшой аванс до завтра.
'I need a small advance until tomorrow.' Viktor finally confesses his urgent monetary need.
Я знаю твои авансы, Виктор.
'I know your advances, Viktor.' Dmitry remains completely unmoved by the plea.
Ни копейки ты не получишь!
'You will not get a single kopeck!' Nagiyev puts the word for 'kopeck' together with 'will get' in a crisp, natural spoken turn of phrase.
Дмитрий, ты пожалеешь об этом!

'Dmitry, you will regret this!' Viktor shouts frustratedly before hanging up. Now, let us listen to the complete scene again to practice your comprehension. Now let's listen to the whole conversation again from start to finish.

A comedic interaction highlighting Dmitry Nagiyev's stubborn refusal to fund Barinov's gambling habits. Next time you watch the episode, listen for the Russian expressions for 'advance' and 'to be' — you will catch every word right away. See you in the next scene.
